precepts.text: Cited as the little sanctuaries the Lord provides in the countries where Israel is scattered, the same as the schools today.
precepts.point: Any task set before our forefathers got done: the Maccabees who were not warriors, the slaves who left Egypt. Egypt was America. If the shooting starts, we know scripturally what happens; the Lord takes care of it.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“So built we the wall”: all through our history, the forefathers were building. What we are doing today is nothing different from what they always did, and Ezekiel shows the kind of building the Lord gives us while we are scattered.

“Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” Israel was cast far off and scattered, and the Lord still gave them little sanctuaries in the lands where they came.

When Paul went to Galatia, to Colossae, to Corinth and to Thessalonica, those were sanctuaries, just like the ones you see today. The schools are those little sanctuaries in the countries, and each and every one of us put a hand into building each and every one of them.

So the wall of Nehemiah and the little sanctuary of Ezekiel are the same work. The people built because they had a mind to work, and that mind to work is what leadership has to put into the people now.

precepts.text: I know the things that come into your mind, every one of them; the Lord knows the spirit behind the sin.
precepts.point: Saying we knew it not does not stand before the Most High. Doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it, and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? A lot of people say they never heard this truth when they heard it and did not want to apply it. The Most High knows the things that come into your mind, every one of them; he created us and knows us better than we know ourselves, and he knows whether you sinned through ignorance or willfully.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
“Thus have ye said, O house of Israel: for I know the things that come into your mind, every one of them.”

The Most High knows the things that come into your mind, every one of them. He created us and knows us better than we know ourselves, and He knows the spirit behind the sin: whether you sinned through ignorance, as the ruler in Leviticus 4, or willfully.

precepts.text: Although I have cast them far off among the heathen and scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.
precepts.point: A lot of us do not like going to the Sabbath, do not like congregating, hear the class and they are out. We have to love the habitation of His house; these are the things that continually build us up.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

precepts.why:
“Lord, I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth.” David is talking about Jerusalem, but we also have little sanctuaries: “Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord God; Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.”

Though He cast us far off among the heathen and scattered us among the countries, He is to us a little sanctuary in the countries where we come. Those are the little congregations in Florida, Georgia, New York, Uganda, France, Russia.

Honor is the keeping of the commandments of God, the love between a husband and wife, making marriages great again. David loved everything that came with keeping the commandments: congregating, seeing your brothers and sisters, going for counsel, getting corrected. A lot of us do not like going to the Sabbath, do not like congregating, hear the class and they are out. We have to love the habitation of His house, because these are the things that continually build us up.

precepts.text: Yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.
precepts.point: The Most High cast us off among the heathen and scattered us among the countries, yet he became to us a little sanctuary in the countries where we come. In these sanctuaries you learn who the ungodly are, who prosper in this world serving Satan, and what their end is.

note.label: Psalm 134: The Servants Blessing the Most High in the Sanctuary

precepts.why:
“Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, and bless the Lord.” The sanctuary is the house of the Most High where you go every Sabbath, the little sanctuaries IUIC has set up. “Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.”

The Most High cast us off among the heathen and scattered us among the countries, yet he became to us a little sanctuary in the countries where we come.

precepts.text: The Most High is a little sanctuary to his people in the countries where they are scattered.
precepts.point: The word became a snare upon the leadership because the understanding is given precept upon precept, in another tongue, so that those without it stumble and fall.

note.label: Isaiah 8: Maher-shalal-hash-baz, the Snare, and the Law and the Testimony

precepts.why:
“And he shall be for a sanctuary”. Ezekiel shows where: “Thus saith the Lord God; Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.”

The Most High is a little sanctuary to his people in the countries where they are scattered. Though he cast them far off among the heathen, he is still their sanctuary there. That is the one side of Isaiah 8:14; the other is that the same one is “a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence” to those who reject him.

precepts.text: The manner of the heathen is the immoral laws and spiritual idolatry that we followed back then and still follow today.
precepts.point: We get judged because we do not keep the Most High's laws, the same then as today; they had not walked in His statutes but had done after the manners of the heathen around about them.

note.label: Ezekiel 11: This City Shall Not Be Your Cauldron

precepts.why:
“ye shall know that I am the Lord: for ye have not walked in my statutes, neither executed my judgments, but have done after the manners of the heathen that are round about you.” The law had warned them: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do: neither shall ye walk in their ordinances.”

The manner of the heathen is the immoral laws and spiritual idolatry that we followed back then and still follow today. We get judged because we do not keep the Most High's laws, the same then as now; so He delivers us into the hands of strangers, the nations, and judges us in the border of Israel, that we may know that He is the Lord.

precepts.text: The cherubims are the angels attached to the wheels, described in the vision of chapter one.
precepts.point: The vision went up from Ezekiel, and he spoke unto the captives in Babylon all the things the Most High had showed him.

note.label: Ezekiel 11: This City Shall Not Be Your Cauldron

precepts.why:
The cherubims that lift up their wings here, with the wheels beside them, are the same living creatures Ezekiel saw at the first. Back in chapter one he beheld “one wheel upon the earth by the living creatures, with his four faces”, their appearance “like unto the colour of a beryl”, and “a wheel in the middle of a wheel.” Their rings “were so high that they were dreadful”, and “full of eyes round about them four.”

The cherubims are the angels attached to the wheels. “when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.” Wherever the spirit was to go, they went, “for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.” When those went, these went; when those stood, these stood.

So when the cherubims lift up their wings and the wheels lift with them, and the glory of the God of Israel is over them above, it is that same vision moving. The glory of the Lord goes up from the midst of the city and stands upon the mountain on the east side, and the spirit then takes Ezekiel in a vision into Chaldea, to them of the captivity, where he speaks to the captives in Babylon all the things the Most High had showed him.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 9 Explained Pt. 2

precepts.why: We don't have the sanctuary today? Then what is this talking about? “Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord God; Although I have cast them far off among the heathen,” We are scattered throughout America, Africa, India, Central and South America, the Caribbean islands. “and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” In all the countries God said, I will be to them a little sanctuary. We will have small schools. This is little right here; you might think this is big, but God says this is little, because the Bible says we number the sand of the sea.

The Most High tells Ezekiel to prophesy against these twenty-five wicked men.
